question.text: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations require that the sponsor and manager of the AIF shall act in a fiduciary capacity and shall:

answer.text: Refuse to invest in any sector where any sponsor employee has personal investments
Disclose all conflicts of interest to investors as and when they arise or seem likely to arise, and establish written policies to identify, monitor and mitigate conflicts
Require a board-level conflict committee in each investee company
Obtain case-by-case approval from SEBI before any investment that may raise conflicts

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.7 (Regulation on Governance Structure in AIF), the SEBI (AIF) Regulations state sponsors/managers shall act in fiduciary capacity, disclose conflicts to investors as and when they arise OR seem likely to arise, and establish written policies to identify, monitor and appropriately mitigate conflicts. They shall abide by high-level principles specified by SEBI. **The Trap:** Option A is overbroad — personal investments don't automatically ban entire sectors. Option C is not the regulatory text. Option D is operationally impractical and not mandated. **Cross-Exam Context:** Fiduciary + disclose + policy trilogy is the common SEBI template — tested identically in XXI-A (PMS) and X-A/X-B (IA). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Keep a running conflicts register at the Manager. Small conflicts that individually seem trivial can cluster into a pattern that SEBI interprets as systemic — disclose early, disclose often.
